C>0 in the fixed-scale theorem, so epsilon=τ/C is feasible once τ is small. The upper fixed-scale value bound gives a penalized trial infimum at most beta_*+τ−τ log(τ/C), tending to beta_*<b. An attained body trial exists by the parent theorem for small scale, though an approximating trial would also suffice.

For 0<epsilon≤bar_epsilon≤1 the penalty is nonnegative, and beta_epsilon≥beta0. Therefore every sufficiently late minimizing pair has a body representative in the original compact sublevel. At fixed τ, nonnegative beta_epsilon and divergent -τ log epsilon exclude epsilon tending to zero along that sequence. The parent's all-normal cap comparison is joint in body and scale and gives attainment on the compact product after restricting to scales bounded away from zero.

Substituting epsilon=τs and comparing the fixed-scale lower bound to the trial cancels beta_*−τ log τ and gives c1 s−log s≤1+log C. Since c1>0 this function tends to +infinity as s approaches zero or infinity. Its sublevel is a compact subset of (0,infinity), independent of τ. Thus epsilon/τ has two positive uniform bounds, and eventually epsilon<bar_epsilon.
At the chosen scale the penalty is independent of the body, so every joint minimizer is a body minimizer among all positive compatible families at that scale, without claiming uniqueness.
